status: written before any CausalArena number for these filters was computed; dev split only; no test split read; no kernel change
design: docs/design/q2_lever_map.md rows L8 (shadow ordering) and L7 (resampling stability as a link filter); section 6 item 1
question: Can a filter withdraw the ledger's false links, above all the shadows (54% of false links), precisely enough to be acted on?
why_now: Headroom ladder: removing false links is worth +0.03 DV-1 precision, +0.12 coverage and +0.14 directed F1 (semantic v3, D); both direction rounds (dirsig-1, dirsig-2) traced their failures back to link errors.

filters.L8a: data-processing inequality on |Spearman|: cut a found link whose dpi_ratio (min over ledger triangles of s(a,b) / min(s(a,m), s(m,b))) is below a cut-off c; links in no triangle are never cut
filters.L8b: the same on binned mutual information, Miller-Madow corrected
filters.L7: resampling stability: share of 10 bootstrap resamples (kernel.harness resample_indices, seed 20261015, B4's draws) whose v3 ledger contains the link; cut below a cut-off theta
filters.L7_or_L8a: secondary: the union of the two cuts, each at its own cross-fitted cut-off

code: kernel/linkfilt.py (tested in tests/test_q2_linkfilt.py on a chain with its shadow), analysis/q2_linkfilt.py

units.links: found links of the v3 ledger (rule C3, Meek R1/R3 open), regime D. L8: all 125 dev files per family. L7: the 25 first-replicate dev files per family (the files B4 resampled; one file per scenario)
units.cut_precision: share of cut links that are false
units.cut_recall: share of the ledger's false links that are cut
units.true_lost: share of the ledger's true found links that are cut

licence_rule.bar: cross-fitted cut precision >= 0.80 and cross-fitted cut recall >= 0.10, in a family
licence_rule.cut_off: per filter and family, the most permissive cut-off (largest c or theta from the grid) whose cut precision on 4 of 5 scenario folds is >= 0.80 with at least 30 cuts; measured on the 5th fold
licence_rule.why_0.80: a cut withdraws a claim; it must be right at least as often as the weakest licence the ledger keeps acting on (Meek R2, 0.75) and match the direction licence bar

answer_level: secondary: on each held-out fold, the ledger's graph with the cuts removed (no re-orientation: directions that relied on a cut link stay as they were) is re-scored for DV-1 precision and coverage and directed F1, against the uncut graph

predictions.P-LF0: Shadows sit in triangles: at least 40% of the ledger's shadow false links are in a ledger triangle, both families. Refuted if below 25% in either.
predictions.P-LF1: L8a does not earn a licence in either family: true triangles (a -> m -> b plus a -> b) are common enough in designed SCMs that the weakest link of a triangle is often real. Refuted if L8a earns a licence in either family.
predictions.P-LF2: L8b's cross-fitted cut precision is within 0.03 of L8a's or above it, both families. Refuted if more than 0.03 below in either.
predictions.P-LF3: Stability separates true from false links overall: the probability that a random true link is more stable than a random false link (AUC) is >= 0.70, both families. Refuted if below 0.60 in either.
predictions.P-LF4: Shadows are stable: among false links, shadows' median stability exceeds unrelated false links' by >= 0.10, both families (a shadow is a systematic consequence of a real path, not noise). Refuted if not in either.
predictions.P-LF5: L7 earns a licence in at least one family, by cutting unstable unrelated and common-cause false links. Refuted if in neither.
predictions.P-LF6: Any licensed filter raises the fold-wise DV-1 precision and directed F1 of the ledger by >= 0.01 in its family. Refuted if a licensed filter lowers either.

failure_modes_named_in_advance: True triangles: a real direct link a -> b next to a real path a -> m -> b can be weaker than both path links; DPI cuts it (this is P-LF1's bet).

Shadows of a missed mediator: when the ledger missed a-m or m-b, the shadow a-b has no triangle and no ordering filter can see it; it also carries the only connection the ledger has between a and b, so cutting it would hurt answers.
Nonlinear and non-monotone links: |Spearman| understates them, so a real non-monotone link can look like the weakest of a triangle (L8b is the guard).
Mutual-information bias differs by column type (discrete vs binned); the estimator is Miller-Madow corrected, and a residual bias is still possible.
Stability can be high for systematic errors: GES re-finds a shadow on every resample if the path is strong (P-LF4's bet), so L7 may cut mostly unrelated links, a minority of false links.
L7 is measured on 25 files per family (one per scenario), so its fold-wise numbers carry more noise than L8's.

Cutting without re-orientation leaves collider directions whose licence used a cut link; the answer-level numbers are therefore a lower bound on what a re-derived ledger would do, and may differ in sign.
outputs: analysis/results/q2_v3/linkfilt_dev.json; analysis/reports/q2_linkfilt_dev.md; lever map rows L7, L8 updated
